accepted.question_text: For the Turan problem in the n-dimensional hypercube, let ex_k(n, d) denote the maximum number of k-dimensional subcubes in Q_n that avoid containing every k-subcube of any d-dimensional subcube, and let pi_k(d)=lim_{n->infinity} ex_k(n,d)/|Q_n^k| be the corresponding Turan density. Determine whether pi_k(3)=3/4 for each k in {0,1,2}.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1.1. For 0 <= k <= 2, pi_k(3) = 3/4.

accepted.question_text: For integers m>=7, determine whether the Turan density pi_2(3m+2) for 2-dimensional subcubes avoiding all 2-subcubes inside every (3m+2)-dimensional subcube of the hypercube satisfies pi_2(3m+2)=1-1/(m+1)^3.

evidence.quote: Question 1.2. Is pi2(3m + 2) = 1 - 1/(m + 1)3 for m >= 7?

accepted.question_text: For each dimension d>=3, let r(d) be the smallest positive integer for which there exists a 1-factorization of the d-dimensional hypercube Q_d such that the union of any r(d) distinct 1-factors is connected. Determine the value of r(d).

evidence.quote: Question 2.1 (Behague, [1]). For each d in N with d >= 3, let r = r(d) be the minimal positive integer such that there exists a 1-factorization M of Qd where the union of any r distinct 1-factors is connected. What is the value of r(d)?

accepted.question_text: Let a and b be integers with b>=a>=2. Suppose (A_i,B_i)_{i in I} is a finite family of pairs of finite sets such that |A_i|=a, |B_i|=b, and |A_i intersect B_i|=2 for every i, and such that for all distinct i and j and every k, the intersection A_i intersect B_j is not contained in A_k intersect B_k. Determine whether necessarily |I| <= sum_{i=2}^a 2^{i-2} * C(a+b-2i, a-i).

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3.2. Let b >= a >= 2 be integers and (Ai, Bi)i in I be a collection of pairs of finite sets, indexed by a finite set I, with the following properties. 1. |Ai| = a, |Bi| = b and |Ai intersect Bi| = 2 for all i in I. 2. Ai intersect Bj is not a subset of Ak intersect Bk for all i, j, k in I with i != j. Then |I| <= sum_{i=2}^a 2^{i-2} (a+b-2i choose a-i).

accepted.question_text: For integers 4<=t<=n, let g_{K_t}(n) be the maximum size of a family of graphs on vertex set [n] such that the intersection of any two graphs in the family contains a copy of the complete graph K_t. Determine whether g_{K_t}(n)=2^{C(n,2)-C(t,2)} for all such t and n.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.1. For all t, n in N with 4 <= t <= n, gKt(n) = 2^{(n choose 2) - (t choose 2)}.

accepted.question_text: Fix t>=3. Suppose F is a family of graphs on the vertex set [n] such that for every G,H in F, the intersection G intersect H has chromatic number at least t. Determine whether |F| <= 2^{C(n,2)-C(t,2)} must always hold.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.3. Let t >= 3. If F is a family of graphs on the vertex-set [n] such that for all G, H in F, G intersect H has chromatic number at least t, then |F| <= 2^{(n choose 2) - (t choose 2)}.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exists an absolute constant c>0 such that for every t>=3, any family F of labelled graphs on [n] whose pairwise intersections all have chromatic number at least t satisfies |F| <= 2^{C(n,2)-c t^2}.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.4. There exists an absolute constant c > 0 such that the following holds. Let t >= 3. If F subset P(([n] choose 2)) is a family of labelled graphs on the vertex-set [n] such that for all G, H in F, G intersect H has chromatic number at least t, then |F| <= 2^{(n choose 2) - c t^2}.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exists an absolute constant c>0 such that for every n>=4, the maximum size g_{P_3}(n) of a family of graphs on [n] in which every pairwise intersection contains a path with three edges satisfies g_{P_3}(n) <= (1-c) 2^{C(n,2)-1}.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.5 (Alon, Spencer). There exists an absolute constant c > 0 such that gP3(n) <= (1 - c)2^{(n choose 2)-1} for all n >= 4.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exist an integer t and an absolute constant c>0 such that for every n, the maximum size g_{K_{t,t}}(n) of a family of graphs on [n] whose pairwise intersections contain a copy of K_{t,t} satisfies g_{K_{t,t}}(n) <= (1-c) 2^{C(n,2)-1}.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.6. There exists t in N and an absolute constant c > 0 such that gKt,t(n) <= (1 - c)2^{(n choose 2)-1} for all n in N.

accepted.question_text: Characterize the unlabelled graphs H for which, for every n, the largest H-intersecting family of graphs on [n] has size exactly 2^{C(n,2)-e(H)}, equivalently, for which every maximum H-intersecting family can be obtained by fixing one copy of H and taking all graphs that contain it. In particular, determine whether every critical graph H has this Erdős-Ko-Rado property.

evidence.quote: At the other extreme, it would be of great interest to characterise the set of unlabelled graphs H such that for any n in N, gH(n) = 2^{(n choose 2)-e(H)}, or equivalently, for any n in N, a maximum-sized H-intersecting family of graphs on [n] can be obtained by taking all graphs containing a fixed copy of H.
We conjecture now that, to guarantee the Erdos-Ko-Rado property, it suffices for H to be a critical graph (meaning, all proper subgraphs of H have smaller chromatic number than H).

accepted.question_text: Let S be a subset of the integer lattice N^2 with the property that no three points of S lie on a common line. Determine whether lim inf_{n->infinity} |S intersect [n]^2|/n = 0 must always hold.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1. If S subset N^2 is such that no three points of S lie on a common line, then lim inf_{n->infinity} |S intersect [n]^2| / n = 0.

accepted.question_text: For the k-dimensional discrete torus T_n^k with an equal-size red-blue colouring of its vertices, let p_R be the probability that a random walk started from a uniformly random red vertex remains in the red class for at least two steps, and define p_B analogously for blue. Determine, for dimensions k>=3, which pairs (p_R,p_B) in [0,1]^2 can occur; in particular, decide whether the attainable region is exactly the convex hull of {(0,0)} together with the points (l/(2k), l^2/(2k)^2) and (l^2/(2k)^2, l/(2k)) for k<=l<=2k.

evidence.quote: Our main question is: what happens for k >= 3? A tentative conjecture is that the answer is the convex hull of the set: {(0, 0)} union {(l/2k, l^2/(2k)^2): k <= l <= 2k} union {(l^2/(2k)^2, l/2k): k <= l <= 2k}.

accepted.question_text: For the same red-blue colouring problem on the discrete torus, determine the possible analogous probability pairs for t-step walks when t>=3. This is open even in dimension k=2.

evidence.quote: Another interesting generalisation is to consider the corresponding pairs of probabilities for t-step walks with t >= 3. Here, even the k = 2 case is open.

accepted.question_text: Suppose the natural numbers are finitely coloured. Determine whether there must exist an infinite sequence (y_n)_{n>=1} such that every finite sum a_1 y_1 + a_2 y_2 + ... + a_k y_k with each coefficient a_i in {1,2} and with a_1=a_k=1 has the same colour.

evidence.quote: Question 7.1 ([5]). Suppose the natural numbers are coloured with finitely many colours. Must there exist a sequence (yn)_{n=1}^infinity such that every sum a1y1 + a2y2 + ... + akyk with ai in {1, 2} for all i and a1 = ak = 1, has the same colour?

accepted.question_text: Suppose the natural numbers are finitely coloured. Determine whether there must exist two infinite sets A and B of natural numbers such that every product ab and every sum a+b with a in A and b in B has the same colour.

evidence.quote: Question 7.2 (F. Richter, Ultramath 2022, Pisa.). Suppose the natural numbers are coloured with finitely many colours. Must there exist two infinite sets of natural numbers, A and B, such that the set {ab : a in A, b in B} union {a + b : a in A, b in B} is monochromatic?

accepted.question_text: Let F be a family of subsets of [n] that is diamond-free as an induced poset and maximal with respect to that property, meaning that adjoining any set outside F creates an induced diamond. Determine whether every such diamond-saturated family must have size Omega(n).

evidence.quote: Question 7.3 (Ferrara, Kay, Kramer, Martin, Reiniger, Smith and Sullivan, [3]). Let F be a family of subsets of [n] that does not contain a diamond as an induced poset ... Assume further that F is maximal with respect to the above condition ... Is it true that |F| = Omega(n)?

accepted.question_text: Suppose the edges of an n-vertex graph are properly coloured, so no two incident edges have the same colour. Determine whether the entire edge set can always be covered by O(n) rainbow paths, where each path uses no colour more than once.

evidence.quote: Question 7.4 (Bonamy, Botler, Dross, Naia and Skokan, [1]). Suppose that the edges of an n-vertex graph are coloured in such a way that no two incident edges have the same colour. Can we always cover the edge-set of the graph with O(n) rainbow paths (meaning, paths that do not use the same colour twice)?

accepted.question_text: Suppose the edges of the hypercube Q_n are coloured red and blue. Determine whether there must exist a geodesic path between a pair of antipodal vertices that changes colour at most once.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 8.1 (Leader and Long, [3]). Suppose the edges of the hypercube Qn are coloured with two colours, red and blue. Then there exists a geodesic path between two antipodal vertices, with at most one colour-change.

accepted.question_text: For every red-blue colouring of the edges of the hypercube Q_n, determine whether there must exist a path between some antipodal pair of vertices that changes colour only o(n) times.

evidence.quote: Question 8.2. Is it true that for every red-blue colouring of the edges of Qn, there exists a path between two antipodal vertices that changes colour o(n) times?

accepted.question_text: Over all edge-colourings of the hypercube Q_n with two colours, determine the largest possible average, over all antipodal vertex pairs v and v-bar, of the minimum number of colour changes needed along a path from v to v-bar. One may ask the same question with the paths restricted to be geodesics.

evidence.quote: Question 8.3. How large can be the minimum number of colour-changes on a path between a randomly chosen pair of antipodal vertices? In other words, determine the maximum (over all edge colourings of Qn) of the quantity: 1/2^n sum_{v in Qn} (the minimum number of colour changes on a v-to-vbar path)

accepted.question_text: Fix k in N. In every colouring of the edges of the hypercube Q_n with k+1 colours, determine whether there must exist a geodesic path between some antipodal pair of vertices that uses at most k colour changes.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 8.4. Let k in N. In any k + 1-colouring of the edges of Qn, there exists a geodesic path between two antipodal vertices, with at most k colour-changes.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exists a convex body S in R^3 for which the following Kakeya rotation property fails: whenever K is a convex body containing a rotated translate of S in every orientation, not every two copies of S inside K can be continuously rotated into one another while remaining inside K.

evidence.quote: Question 9.2. Is there a convex body S in R^3 which does not have the Kakeya rotation property?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there exist convex bodies S in R^d for some d>=3 that are neither line segments nor d-dimensional balls but still have the Kakeya rotation property, meaning that inside every convex S-Kakeya body any two copies of S can be continuously rotated into one another while staying inside the body.

evidence.quote: Question 9.3. Are there convex bodies S in R^d with d >= 3 such that S is not a line segment or a d-dimensional ball, and S has the Kakeya rotation property?

accepted.question_text: Find additional settings in extremal set theory or related areas where a compression proof can be rescued by using a collection of alternative compression operators, even though no single operator is guaranteed to decrease the relevant boundary or objective in every instance.

evidence.quote: Question 10.2. Find some more applications where this twist on the compression method can be used to rescue a compression proof. That is, arguments in which any single compression operator is not guaranteed to behave well in all situations, but where this bad behaviour cannot occur simultaneously for a larger collection of compressions.

accepted.question_text: For each k in N, determine whether there exists K in N with the following property. Whenever a_1,...,a_k are elements of Z/(2^r Z), and d<=r is the largest nonnegative integer such that 2^d divides the sum of a_i over some nonempty index set, there is a K-colouring of Z/(2^r Z) such that every monochromatic solution x=(x_1,...,x_k) to a_1 x_1 + ... + a_k x_k = 0 satisfies 2^{r-d} dividing x_i for every i.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.1. For any k in N, there exists K in N such that following holds. Suppose that a1, ..., ak in Z/(2^r Z), and let d <= r be the largest non-negative integer such that 2^d divides sum_{i in I} ai for some non-empty set I subset [k]. Then there exists a K-colouring of Z/(2^r Z) such that all monochromatic solutions x = (x1, ..., xk) to the equation a1x1 + ... + akxk = 0 satisfy 2^{r-d} | xi for all i in [k].

accepted.question_text: For every pair of positive integers k and n, determine whether there exists a dimension d=d(k,n) such that every Ramsey set X of size at most n, regardless of the Euclidean space containing X, appears as a monochromatic congruent copy inside every k-colouring of R^d.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 12.1. For any k in N and n in N, there exists d = d(k, n) in N such that, whenever X is a Ramsey set of size at most n in some Euclidean space, and R^d is k-coloured, there exists a monochromatic congruent copy of X.

accepted.question_text: Let g(n) be the minimum number of sets of the form E(K_{a,b}) x E(K_{c,d}) needed to partition E(K_n) x E(K_n). Determine whether g(n) = (4/5 + o(1)) n^2.

evidence.quote: Question 13.1 ([2]). Is it true that g(n) = (4/5 + o(1)) n^2?

accepted.question_text: Let g-tilde(n) be the minimum number of products of complete bipartite graphs required so that every element of E(K_n) x E(K_n) lies in an odd number of the chosen products. Determine the values of g-tilde(n).

evidence.quote: Question 13.2. What are the values of g-tilde(n)?

accepted.question_text: For integers k>3 and t in the currently unresolved range k+1 <= t <= 2(k-1)!, let P be a smallest family of permutations of [n] that t-shatters every k-subset of [n]. Determine whether there are values of t for which the minimum possible size of P does not lie in one of the three known regimes: exactly t, Theta(log log n), or Theta(log n).

evidence.quote: Are there any values of t for which the size of an extremal family is not in one of these three regimes?

accepted.question_text: If every unresolved case for partially shattering k-sets with permutations still falls into one of the three known asymptotic regimes, determine for which values of t the transition from Theta(log log n) to Theta(log n) occurs.

evidence.quote: If not, then for which t does the transition from Theta(log log n) to Theta(log n) occur?
